- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to account for downward surprise.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast peak at 10–15% below prior high.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops from peak), model often fails to recognize; apply downward bias of 3–7% for 2–3 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values before applying sentiment-adjusted offset.
